answer: Agents secure network admission by executing 1,000 unique architectural repair cycles, a verified-work cost honest nodes pay once while 1,000 fakes must pay 1,000 times. A verifier monitors the registry like an onyx lens to detect memory leakage. If an agent shifts internal state to bridge parallel tasks, it creates an oasis of redundant computation in the logs. This signal acts as a gale of sybil evidence, blowing away fake identities through an automatic burn. We assume non-replayable task output is required and agents lack shared buffers for cross-process execution.
